{{short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:Chaim Goodman-Strauss.jpg|thumb|Chaim Goodman-Strauss assembling sculpture at Gathering 4 Gardner, Atlanta, GA, 2008.]]

'''Chaim Goodman-Strauss''' (born June 22, 1967 in Austin, Texas) is an American mathematician who works in [[convex geometry]], especially [[aperiodic tiling]]. He retired from the faculty of the [[University of Arkansas]] and currently serves as outreach mathematician for the [[National Museum of Mathematics]]. He is co-author with [[John H. Conway]] and Heidi Burgiel of ''[[The Symmetries of Things]]'', a comprehensive book surveying the mathematical theory of patterns.<ref>[https://plus.maths.org/content/symmetries-things Review of ''The symmetries of things''], by Phil Wilson, [[Plus Magazine]], December 1, 2008:  "The book presents a whole new way of looking at patterns. The methods have been worked out so exhaustively, and the trails opened up in the book have been followed so extensively, that you almost can't believe that such a huge body of knowledge could have lain dormant for so long!"</ref>

==Education and career==
Goodman-Strauss received both his B.S. (1988) and Ph.D. (1994) in mathematics from the [[University of Texas at Austin]].<ref name=collegeboard>[https://www.collegeboard.org/node/12446 Chaim Goodman-Strauss] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190901111547/https://www.collegeboard.org/node/12446 |date=2019-09-01 }} The College Board</ref> His doctoral advisor was [[John Edwin Luecke]].<ref name="nodak">{{cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=13187|title=Chaim Goodman-Strauss - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|accessdate=2018-01-01}}</ref> He joined the faculty at the [[University of Arkansas, Fayetteville]] (UA) in 1994 and served as departmental chair from 2008 to 2015. He held visiting positions at the  [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] and [[Princeton University]].<ref name=collegeboard/><ref>[http://www.celebrationofmind.org/?project=chaim-goodman-strauss Gathering for Gardner] Celebration of Mind Presenter</ref>

During 1995 he did research at [[The Geometry Center]], a mathematics research and education center at the [[University of Minnesota]], where he investigated aperiodic tilings of the plane.<ref>[http://www.geom.uiuc.edu/about/people/home/strauss.html Chaim Goodman-Strauss: Activities at the Geometry Center] University Of Minnesota</ref>

Goodman-Strauss has been fascinated by patterns and mathematical paradoxes for as long as he can remember. He attended a lecture about the mathematician [[Georg Cantor]] when he was 17 and says, "I was already doomed to be a mathematician, but that lecture sealed my fate."<ref>''[https://researchfrontiers.uark.edu/the-shape-of-everyday-things/ The Shape of Everyday Things]'' by Melissa Lutz Blouin. Research News, Spring 2005</ref> He became a mathematics writer and popularizer. From 2004 to 2012, in conjunction with [[KUAF|KUAF 91.3 FM]], the University of Arkansas [[NPR]] affiliate, he presented "[http://mathfactor.uark.edu/ The Math Factor]," a podcast website dealing with recreational mathematics.<ref name=factor>[http://mathfactor.uark.edu/about/ The Math Factor Podcast Website] July 24, 2012</ref> He is an admirer of [[Martin Gardner]] and is on the advisory council of [[Gathering 4 Gardner]], an organization that celebrates the legacy of the famed mathematics popularizer and [[Scientific American]] columnist,<ref name=g4g>[https://www.gathering4gardner.org/about/ About The G4G Foundation] Gathering 4 Gardner</ref> and is active in the associated [[Celebration of Mind]] events.<ref>[http://www.celebrationofmind.org/project/chaim-goodman-strauss Presenter: Chaim Goodman-Strauss] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190901113039/http://www.celebrationofmind.org/project/chaim-goodman-strauss |date=2019-09-01 }} Celebration of Mind</ref><ref>[http://www.celebrationofmind.org/archives/1357 Doubly Marked Robinson Tiles] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190901114554/http://www.celebrationofmind.org/archives/1357 |date=2019-09-01 }} Celebration of Mind</ref> In 2022 Goodman-Strauss was awarded the National Museum of Mathematics' [https://momath.org/rosenthal-prize/ Rosenthal Prize], which recognizes innovation and inspiration in math teaching.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-01-10 |title=$25K prize awarded for middle school math lesson developed by UA professor |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2022/jan/10/25k-prize-for-middle-school-math-lesson-developed/ |access-date=2023-06-02 |website=Arkansas Online |language=en}}</ref>

==Aperiodic monotiles==
[[File:Smith_aperiodic_monotiling.svg|thumb|A tiling that does not repeat and uses only one shape, discovered by [[David Smith (hobbyist)|David Smith]].]]
On Mar 20, 2023 Strauss, together with [[David Smith (hobbyist)|David Smith]], Joseph Samuel Myers and [[Craig S. Kaplan]], announced the proof that the tile discovered by David Smith is an aperiodic monotile,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Roberts |first=Siobhan |date=2023-03-28 |title=Elusive 'Einstein' Solves a Longstanding Math Problem |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/03/28/science/mathematics-tiling-einstein.html |access-date=2023-06-02 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> i.e., a solution to a longstanding open [[einstein problem]].<ref>{{cite journal | arxiv=2303.10798 | last1=Smith | first1=David | author2=Joseph Samuel Myers | last3=Kaplan | first3=Craig S. | last4=Goodman-Strauss | first4=Chaim | title=An aperiodic monotile | journal=Combinatorial Theory | year=2024 | volume=4 | doi=10.5070/C64163843  | doi-access=free}}</ref> The team continues to refine this work.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Roberts |first=Siobhan |date=2023-06-01 |title=With a New, Improved 'Einstein,' Puzzlers Settle a Math Problem |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/06/01/science/puzzles-mathematics-tiling.html |access-date=2023-06-02 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

==Mathematical artist==
In 2008 Goodman-Strauss teamed up with [[J. H. Conway]] and Heidi Burgiel to write ''[[The Symmetries of Things]]'', an exhaustive and reader-accessible overview of the mathematical theory of patterns. He produced hundreds of full-color images for this book using software that he developed for the purpose.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/mathimagery/thumbnails.php?album=17 Chaim Goodman-Strauss :: Symmetries] AMS:  Mathematical Imagery</ref>  The Mathematical Association of America said, "The first thing one notices when one picks up a copy … is that it is a beautiful book … filled with gorgeous color pictures … many of which were generated by Goodman-Strauss. Unlike some books which add in illustrations to keep the reader's attention, the pictures are genuinely essential to the topic of this book."<ref name=glass>[https://www.maa.org/publications/maa-reviews/the-symmetries-of-things Review of ''The symmetries of things''], by Darren Glass, [[The Mathematical Association of America]], July 10, 2008</ref>

He also creates large-scale sculptures inspired by mathematics, and some of these have been featured at Gathering 4 Gardner conferences.<ref>[http://mathfactor.uark.edu/ The Math Factor Podcast Website] Pictures from the Gathering</ref>
